definitions.explanation: Having a tendency to quickly lose interest in things and shift attention to something new. Can describe personality, tastes, or feelings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧だ。
{移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な⟦{消費者|しょうひしゃ}→消費者：09866_shouhisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ニーズ→ニーズ：11244_niizu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{応|こた}える→応える：09893_kotaeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。
examples.english: It's difficult to meet the needs of fickle consumers.

examples.japanese: ⟦{趣味|しゅみ}→趣味：00889_shumi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ころころ→ころころ：05944_korokoro⟧⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な⟦ところ→ところ：01137_tokoro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧だ。
examples.english: The reason my hobbies keep changing is that I have a fickle streak.

notes:
Literally "transferring spirit" — the idea that one's interest or heart easily moves to something new. Can be used as both a na-adjective ({移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な) and a noun ({移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}). Often carries a mildly negative connotation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧: fickle personality
- {移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a fickle person
- {移|うつ}り{気|ぎ}な⟦{心|こころ}→心：01321_kokoro⟧: a fickle heart

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{気|き}まぐれ→気まぐれ：07319_kimagure⟧: whimsical, capricious — similar but more playful; often used for spontaneous actions
- ⟦{浮気|うわき}→浮気：13285_uwaki⟧: infidelity, fickleness in love — specifically about romantic unfaithfulness
- ⟦{飽|あ}きっぽい→飽きっぽい：20351_akippoi⟧: easily bored — focuses on losing interest quickly
